title: Copper and brass cleaning paste
subtitle: A salt, flour, and vinegar paste for tarnished copper and brass
excerpt: Copper and brass cleaning paste is a soft abrasive paste made from table salt, plain flour, and white vinegar, mixed to a thick consistency. Rubbed onto tarnished copper or brass, it cuts through surface oxidation and restores a warm shine without scratching the metal. Makes about 100 g per batch; mix fresh each time and discard the rest.
sourceNotes: Salt and vinegar cleaning of copper: documented in Mrs Beeton's Book of Household Management (1861) and repeated in Natural Cleaning Solutions by Rachel Ogden (2012). The acetic acid in vinegar reacts with copper oxide (the tarnish) to dissolve it; salt acts as a mild abrasive; flour thickens the paste to improve contact time. Not suitable for lacquered copper finishes or copper-plated items, the paste will strip the lacquer.

recipe.yieldDescription: ~100 g of cleaning paste (enough for 3 to 5 copper or brass pieces)
recipe.batchNotes: Mix fresh per cleaning session. The paste ferments within a few hours as the flour hydrates fully and starts to work, use immediately or within 30 minutes of mixing.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Do not make ahead. Mix immediately before use.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Use within 30 minutes of mixing. Discard any remaining paste, it does not keep.

content.text: Copper and brass cleaning paste is a thick paste of table salt, plain flour, and white vinegar. Rubbed onto tarnished copper or brass, it cuts through the dark surface oxide and restores a warm shine without scratching. Mix fresh per session, the paste does not keep.
Not suitable for lacquered copper or copper-plated items, the acid will strip the surface coating.

items.prepNote: fine table salt; the mild abrasive
thickens the paste to keep it in contact with the metal surface
distilled white or white wine vinegar; provides the acetic acid that dissolves the oxide

content.text: Combine the salt and flour in a small bowl. Add the vinegar and stir to a smooth paste, the consistency of thick porridge. Add a splash more vinegar if the paste is too stiff to spread.

Apply a generous amount of paste to the tarnished copper or brass surface. Leave for three to five minutes. Rub vigorously with a soft cloth in circular motions. The tarnish will lift onto the cloth and the metal underneath will brighten. Rinse well with clean water and dry immediately, leaving the metal wet re-tarnishes it quickly. Buff with a dry cloth to bring up the shine.
Discard any unused paste after the cleaning session. Mix fresh for each use.
